title: Degree-zero module biduality on K-flat and K-injective models
statement:
Let $P$ be a commutative ring and $M$ any $P$-module, regarded as the degree-zero complex $M[0]$. All site-based notions below are taken on the one-object ringed site with only identity coverings, whose module sheaves are the $P$-modules. Let $P[0]\to I$ be any K-injective resolution [def-pur-kinjective-complex] and set $V=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(M[0],I)$ using [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. In the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(P)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], there are canonical identifications $QV\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(M[0],P[0])$ and $Q\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(V,I)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_P(R\operatorname{Hom}_P(M[0],P[0]),P[0])$. The formula
$$\delta_I:M[0]\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(V,I),\qquad \delta_I(m)(h)=h(m)$$
is a chain map, and under these identifications $Q\delta_I$ is the canonical bidual morphism: the tensor-Hom transpose of coefficient evaluation after Koszul exchange of the two factors [lem-sfb-ringed-site-duality-maps]. More precisely, for any quasi-isomorphisms $r:F\to M[0]$ and $t:T\to V$ from K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex] with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], which exist by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], put $W=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(F,I)$. Precomposition gives a quasi-isomorphism $r^*:V\to W$ and $W$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(T,I)$ are K-injective. On these models, coefficient evaluation is represented by
$$T\otimes_P F\longrightarrow I,\qquad z\otimes x\longmapsto (r^*t(z))(x)=t(z)(r(x)).$$
After the Koszul exchange $x\otimes z\mapsto(-1)^{|x||z|}z\otimes x$, this pairing equals the transpose of $\delta_I\circ r$ with its Hom variable precomposed by $t$, namely $x\otimes z\mapsto t(z)(r(x))$. The tensor products here are direct-sum total tensor complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and the identifications and equality are in $D(P)$, not merely on cohomology. No projectivity, flatness or finite generation of $M$, no perfectness, and no Noetherianity is assumed; invertibility of the bidual morphism is not asserted.

proof.text: On the one-object site, the products and differentials defining sheaf Hom are exactly the module Hom products in the statement. Since $I$ is K-injective and represents $P[0]$, the definition of derived internal Hom gives canonical identifications $QV=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(M[0],P[0])$ and $QB=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(QV,P[0])$, where $B=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(V,I)$. This second calculation resolves the target only; it requires no K-flatness or K-injectivity of $V$.

proof.text: Define $\delta_I$ in degree zero by $m\mapsto(h\mapsto h(m))$ and use the zero map in every other degree. Each component is $P$-linear. For homogeneous $h\in V^q$, the Hom differential gives $(d_Vh)(m)=d_I(h(m))$, since $d_{M[0]}=0$. Therefore $(d_B\delta_I(m))(h)=d_I(h(m))-(d_Vh)(m)=0$. Thus this is a chain map into the actual product-defined complex $B$, for an arbitrary, possibly unbounded resolution $I$.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), specialized to the one-object ringed site

proof.text: Choose $r:F\to M[0]$ and $t:T\to V$ using the K-flat resolution theorem, with flat terms as required. Apply resolution independence with target map $1_I$ and source map $r$: it gives the quasi-isomorphism $r^*:V\to W$. Apply the same result with source map $t$: it gives a quasi-isomorphism $s=t^*:B\to B_T$, where $B_T=\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(T,I)$. The K-flat-to-K-injective Hom theorem applied separately to $(F,I)$ and $(T,I)$ makes $W$ and $B_T$ K-injective. No assertion that $V$ itself is K-injective is needed.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), specialized to the one-object ringed site

proof.text: Apply the normalized chain-transpose theorem with its variables $(A,P,E,f)=(V,F,I,r^*)$. The morphism $Qr^*$ is the canonical representative identification for $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(M[0],P[0])$ after the isomorphism $Qr$; hence its uncurrying is coefficient evaluation on these models. Precomposing its first factor with $t$ gives exactly the chain map $c:T\otimes_P F\to I$, $c(z\otimes x)=(r^*t(z))(x)=t(z)(r(x))$. The theorem identifies its localization with derived evaluation after $Qt$ and $Qr$; it states compatibility with inversion of representative quasi-isomorphisms. In particular this identifies the morphism in the derived category, rather than only its effect on cohomology.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), specialized to the one-object ringed site

proof.text: Let $\alpha=s\delta_I:M[0]\to B_T$. Apply the same chain-transpose theorem with $(A,P,E,f)=(M[0],T,I,\alpha)$. Its transpose is $a:M[0]\otimes_P T\to I$, $a(m\otimes z)=t(z)(m)$. Consequently the transpose of $\alpha r$ is $a(r\otimes1_T)$, sending $x\otimes z$ to $t(z)(r(x))$. On the other hand Koszul exchange followed by $c$ sends a homogeneous $x\otimes z$, with degrees $p,q$, to $(-1)^{pq}t(z)(r(x))$. If $p\ne0$ then $r(x)=0$; if $p=0$ then $(-1)^{pq}=1$. The two maps are therefore equal on every tensor summand and thus on their direct-sum totalization.

source.place: Tags 0A90 (lemma-compose), 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined), 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate), specialized to the one-object ringed site

proof.text: The ringed-site duality-maps theorem characterizes $b_{QM[0]}$ as the transpose of coefficient evaluation after Koszul exchange. Let $\kappa: R\operatorname{Hom}_P(QV,P[0])\to R\operatorname{Hom}_P(QT,P[0])$ be precomposition by $Qt$. Under step 1 and the target model $B_T$, resolution independence identifies $\kappa$ with $Qs$. Steps 4 and 5 identify the transpose of $\kappa b_{QM[0]}Qr$ with that of $Q\alpha Qr$, as morphisms $QF\to QB_T$. Bijectivity of the tensor-Hom correspondence gives $\kappa b_{QM[0]}Qr=Q\alpha Qr=Qs\,Q\delta_I\,Qr$. Cancel the isomorphisms $Qr$ and $Qs=\kappa$ to obtain $b_{QM[0]}=Q\delta_I$ under step 1. Naturality and inversion compatibility are exactly those of the cited chain-transpose theorem. These are equalities in $D(P)$ for every choice of the two resolutions; no finiteness, perfectness or Noetherian hypothesis enters.
